title: Unified Contrastive Learning in Image-Text-Label Space
layout_note: Four panels (a)-(d) in a row, each the same structure: two encoders at the bottom, their feature matrices, a product, and a target matrix on top with the label arrow; the paper's own method is (a).
grouping: Panels separated by whitespace with captions (a)-(d) underneath; encoders green (visual) and blue (text / embedding).
shapes_depth: Flat rounded boxes; target matrices as small grids with the positive cells tinted.
proposed_highlight: The paper's method is the first panel, captioned '(Ours)'; the others are the baselines drawn the same way.
lesson: Compare objectives by drawing each as the same two-tower-plus-target-matrix panel, so only the positive pattern differs.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue CVPR 2022 (not verified in this session). Card written while studying arrangement (2026-11-15).

arrangement.units: four panels of identical structure separated by whitespace, each captioned below
arrangement.inputs_as: the words Images / Language under each encoder
arrangement.losses_at: the target matrix with its positives on top of each panel

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: four identical panels side by side, each two encoders at the bottom whose feature matrices meet in a product and a target matrix with its positive cells on top; ours (UniCL) is the first panel

relations.form: in every panel the two sides' feature matrices (U, V / W / U') converge on a product U^T V over a grid whose orange cells mark the positive pairs, labels arrow entering from above
each panel reads bottom to top: input words (Images / Language) -> encoder box -> feature matrix symbol -> product -> target matrix
panel (c) repeats a visual encoder on both sides and its target matrix is twice as wide (|B| x 2|B|)

channels.colour: encoder fill = modality (green visual encoder, blue text encoder or label embedding); orange cells in the target matrices = positive pairs
channels.shape: rounded boxes are encoders, grids are target matrices whose shape (|B|x|B|, |B|xK, |B|x2|B|) is drawn to scale, matrices otherwise appear only as typeset symbols
channels.frame: no frames; panels separated by whitespace and captions (a)-(d)

quality.strengths: Identical panel structure means the only thing that differs is the positive pattern in the target grid, which is exactly the comparison; matrix shapes are drawn to proportion; colour carries modality only.
quality.weaknesses: Ours is placed first rather than last and is marked only by '(Ours)' in a caption; representations U, V are typeset formulas rather than drawn embeddings; no real images or text samples appear.

insights.structure: Four identical tower panels side by side, (a) UniCL (ours), (b) cross entropy, (c) supervised contrast, (d) CLIP/ALIGN, each with two encoders at the bottom, their feature matrices, the product U^T V and a target grid on top.
insights.data: Encoders are flat rounded rectangles (green visual, blue text/embedding), features are typeset matrices with dimension sets (U in R^{P x |B|}), and the target is a small grid whose positive cells are tinted orange.
insights.emphasis: Only the pattern of orange cells and the right-hand encoder change across panels, so the reader compares the positive patterns directly; ours is first and named in the caption.
insights.flow: Each panel reads bottom-up from 'Images'/'Language' through the encoders to the product and the grid, with a 'Labels' arrow dropping in from the top; light grey arrows only.
insights.avoid: The panels are separated only by whitespace and the method is marked only by '(Ours)' in a caption, so the proposed panel has no visual weight over the baselines.
